description: CONCERNS 2 + 3 (coupled: same invoke/planner surface). Add a HARD 3.5s wall-clock per-tick timeout around the model+tools call in unified_agent.invoke() that falls through to the existing rule-based fallback on timeout; cap tool-use iterations at MAX 2 per tick via the Strands per-invocation Limits `turns` cap; disable boto automatic retries (max_attempts=1) on the BedrockModel; add a ~1s per-MCP-tool timeout; and apply the SAME timeout to planner.select_strategy's LLM call (design dependency #7). Make the invoke path testable WITHOUT AWS by adding an injectable agent_factory to unified_agent.register(), mirroring the planner's existing DI. Depends on FEAT-001 (startup must work).
steps: TEST FIRST (constants): add tests/test_constants.py asserting bedrock_model_kwargs() returns model_id + a boto_client_config with retries max_attempts==1 and NO guardrail keys when BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID is unset (env-patched, pure).

In src/agents/players/constants.py add TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3.5, MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS=2, PER_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1.0, env readers GUARDRAIL_ID=os.environ.get('BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID') and GUARDRAIL_VERSION=os.environ.get('BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION','DRAFT'), and bedrock_model_kwargs() returning {'model_id': MODEL_ID, 'boto_client_config': Config(retries={'max_attempts':1,'mode':'standard'})} plus guardrail_id/guardrail_version only when GUARDRAIL_ID is set. Import botocore.config.Config lazily inside the helper so pure constant reads don't require botocore.

TEST FIRST (invoke): add tests/test_unified_agent_invoke.py. Use mock_agentcore_gateway() from test_helpers BEFORE importing unified_agent. Call register(fake_app, player_id, agent_factory=<fake>) (add the agent_factory param), drive invoke via asyncio.run over the async generator, and cover: (a) a fake agent that sleeps past the timeout (patch TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS small) -> returns the deterministic position fallback promptly; (b) a fake agent returning a valid command string -> returns the parsed LLM command; (c) a fake agent that raises -> fallback. Never import real strands.

In src/agents/players/unified_agent.py: add an injectable agent_factory param to register() (default None -> build Agent(BedrockModel(**constants.bedrock_model_kwargs()), ...) as today). In the async invoke(), run the blocking agent call via asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, lambda: agent(state_summary)) wrapped in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=constants.TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS); on asyncio.TimeoutError log and fall through to fallback_fn then last_resort. Pass the iteration cap using the Strands per-invocation Limits `turns` cap (MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS) — confirm the exact call signature against the installed strands-agents>=1.13.0 (likely agent(prompt, limits={'turns': 2})) and record the real signature in findings. Use the default executor (no per-tick thread that is never joined).

Add a generic, injectable per-MCP-tool timeout wrapper (~PER_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) applied to cached_tools at register() time, preserving each tool's name/schema; on tool timeout surface a benign failed-tool-call result so the Strands loop produces a final answer or the tick times out into the fallback. TEST FIRST: a fake tool that blocks > the (patched-small) timeout returns/raises the timeout sentinel within ~the timeout.

Apply the SAME timeout to planner.select_strategy's agent(prompt) call (dependency #7): wrap it so a slow strategy call falls back to rule_based_strategy. Share ONE timeout helper between invoke and the planner (DRY). Build planner._default_agent() via BedrockModel(**constants.bedrock_model_kwargs()). TEST FIRST: extend tests/test_planner.py with an agent_factory whose agent blocks past a patched-small timeout -> select_strategy returns the rule-based strategy.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_unified_agent_invoke.py` passes, including the slow-model case returning the deterministic fallback well under 5s.
Tool-use iterations are capped at 2 per tick via the Strands Limits turns cap; retries are disabled (max_attempts=1) on the BedrockModel.
A per-MCP-tool ~1s timeout prevents one slow tool from consuming the tick budget (unit-tested with a fake blocking tool).
planner.select_strategy's LLM call is bounded by the same timeout and falls back to rule_based_strategy on timeout (tested).
verification: uv run pytest -q tests/test_unified_agent_invoke.py tests/test_planner.py tests/test_constants.py
findings: DONE. Suite 52 -> 67 passing via `uv run pytest -q`. CONFIRMED Strands API (docs for strands-agents, matches pinned >=1.13.0 in each agent pyproject.toml): the per-invocation iteration cap is the `Limits` TypedDict passed as the KEYWORD-ONLY arg `limits` to Agent.__call__/invoke_async/stream_async, i.e. `agent(prompt, limits={'turns': 2})`. `Limits.turns` = max agent-loop iterations (one model call + its tool exec = one turn), counted against len(metrics.latest_agent_invocation.cycles); on trip the loop stops gracefully with stop_reason 'limit_turns' (NO exception). A bad key or non-positive-int value raises TypeError. Other keys: output_tokens, total_tokens (soft caps). BedrockModel kwargs confirmed by context.json (unchanged this FEAT): model_id, boto_client_config (botocore Config), guardrail_id, guardrail_version. constants.bedrock_model_kwargs() now returns {model_id, boto_client_config=Config(retries={'max_attempts':1,'mode':'standard'})} + guardrail_id/guardrail_version ONLY when BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID is set (version defaults 'DRAFT'); botocore.config.Config imported lazily inside the helper so pure constant reads need no botocore. Added constants: TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3.5, MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS=2, PER_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1.0, and guardrail_id()/guardrail_version() env readers (read at CALL time, not import, so env-patched tests stay pure). NEW shared module src/agents/players/runtime_guards.py: call_with_timeout(fn, timeout) (ThreadPoolExecutor-backed sync wall-clock primitive, daemon workers, re-raises callable's own exceptions, raises builtin TimeoutError past deadline) + wrap_tool_with_timeout(tool, timeout) returning a _TimeoutTool proxy that mirrors tool_name/tool_spec/tool_type and on timeout returns a benign {'status':'error','content':[{'text':...}]} result instead of blocking. planner.select_strategy now wraps the agent(prompt) call in call_with_timeout(..., constants.TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and falls back to rule_based_strategy on timeout/any Exception; planner._default_agent() now uses BedrockModel(**constants.bedrock_model_kwargs()). unified_agent.register() gained an injectable agent_factory param (default _default_agent_factory(system_prompt, tools) builds Agent(BedrockModel(**bedrock_model_kwargs()), system_prompt, tools)); cached_tools are wrapped with the per-tool timeout at register time; in invoke() the blocking agent call runs via asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(None, _call_agent) under asyncio.wait_for(timeout=TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and passes limits={'turns': MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS}; on asyncio.TimeoutError it logs and yields the deterministic fallback then returns. DRY: invoke uses the asyncio-native wait_for (it already runs on an event loop); planner + the tool wrapper share the one sync call_with_timeout primitive — same TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS budget. TEST-HELPERS CHANGE later FEATs can reuse: tests/test_helpers.py mock_agentcore_gateway() now also calls a new mock_strands_core() that injects fake top-level `strands` (Agent) + `strands.models` (BedrockModel) modules so `import unified_agent` works offline; the real agent is always replaced via the agent_factory DI on the happy path. TEST NOTE: driving the async invoke via asyncio.run() blocks on shutdown_default_executor() waiting for a timed-out tick's abandoned worker thread; tests use a manual new_event_loop()+run_until_complete()+close() (no executor drain) — the real AgentCore runtime drives invoke on its own loop and never blocks on that drain. New tests: tests/test_constants.py (5), tests/test_runtime_guards.py (5), tests/test_unified_agent_invoke.py (4: valid-command parse, slow-model->fallback under budget, raising-model->fallback, limits turns cap asserted), + 1 planner timeout test. No AWS/Strands network calls were made or needed (all offline via fakes); no read-only deploy checks performed in this FEAT. NOT TOUCHED: guardrails.md, Makefile, .env, ai-team-strands-balanced/, sample-ai-possibilities/. The aws-cdk-lib CfnGuardrail property names and any live read-only deploy confirmations remain for their owning FEATs (FEAT-003/004).
